subject: [Escalation] TideCommerce inference backlog, error spike, and burst authorization
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@tidecommerce.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@tidecommerce.com
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: TideCommerce: sustained latency spike + errors on reserved pool (urgent)

David —

We're seeing a persistent tail-latency increase across our production endpoints since ~07:30 PT and roughly 6% 5xx rate on calls to the /generate route. Token throughput returned as "reserved" in the Console but the real throughput we're getting is ~60% of our committed QPS. This is impacting checkout flows for select merchants. We've attached a snapshot of error traces and the KV cache dump where we see repeated misses.

Can you confirm whether this is on Redwood's side (GPU saturation / kernel issues) or our integration? We need an immediate mitigation plan and an ETA — Tide is pausing a cohort launch at 12:00 PT if this isn't stabilized.

Attachments: tide_error_snapshot_1025.log, kv-cache-dump-1025.json

Thanks,
Sara Li
Head of Platform
TideCommerce
ops@tidecommerce.com

--
On Fri, 23 Oct 2026 at 18:02 Sara Li wrote: "we'll be increasing daily inference volume next week; want to confirm reserved capacity won't regress."
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@tidecommerce.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TideCommerce: sustained latency spike + errors on reserved pool (urgent)

Sara — thanks for the alert and for the logs, really helpful. We're escalating immediately. Short answers up front: (1) we're seeing elevated queue depths on the dedicated GPU pool serving your reserved allocation, (2) there are a small number of kernel/quantization paths that mis-handle a particular long-context workload which increases per-token latency, and (3) we can push a short-term burst allocation while engineering mitigates.

Immediate plan (high level):
- I have looped in Engineering (Irene) and Customer Ops (Marissa).
- We can enable emergency burst (30% extra headroom) within 15–20 minutes if you approve — this will route new traffic to spare capacity in the same region.
- Irene's team will initiate a fast rollback to the prior kernel selection for the affected model variant and enable conservative KV-cache-prefetch for requests with long context.
- We'll also enable aggressive shedding for non-critical log/metric exports to reduce token overhead until the window stabilizes.

Can you confirm: 1) whether Tide wants the burst enabled now, and 2) whether you can accept a short 20-minute routing change (no customer-visible downtime expected) to switch to the fallback model variant? If yes to both, we'll begin immediately and follow up with an incident readout.

-David
David Kim
Enterprise Accounts (Sales) — Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415 555 0192

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TideCommerce: sustained latency spike + errors on reserved pool (urgent)

David / Marissa — digging into the logs Sara attached and our internal telemetry. Quick technical notes:
- We see a kernel selection regression rolled out to that shard at 07:20 PT that degrades attention kernel performance for sequences > 3k tokens; this increases compute per token non-linearly and pushes queue depth up.
- The reserved pool shows a spike in median GPU utilization from 72% -> 94% on a subset of hosts serving Tide. There is very little eviction headroom left.
- KV cache churn is high due to a pattern of many small parallel streams with long context — prefetching reduces misses but increases memory pressure if combined with the newer kernel.

Immediate engineering actions (I can execute now):
1) Roll back kernel selection for model variant tide-prod-v2 -> tide-prod-v1 (expected to drop per-token latency by ~30–40% for long context).
2) Flip route for 10% of traffic to fallback model variant as a canary; if stable, gradually shift more.
3) Initiate emergency burst authorization call with Ops to temporarily allocate GPUs from the shared surge pool. Need approval from Sales / CS for the charge/credit.

Estimate: rollback + 10% canary in ~12–18 minutes; burst allocation if approved in ~20 minutes.

I will not proceed with the full rollback until we have explicit authorization to change routing. Please confirm.

Irene Choi
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: TideCommerce: sustained latency spike + errors on reserved pool (urgent) — stabilized

Sara — quick status update and post-mortem next steps:
- Timeline: we enabled burst + 10% canary at 10:25 PT on 2026-10-25 per your approval. Canary looked stable after 9 minutes; we ramped to 50% then full traffic by 10:42 PT.
- Impact: median p95 tail-latency dropped ~35%; 5xx rate reduced to <0.3%. Reserved throughput restored to >98% of committed QPS.
- Root cause: kernel selection regression for long-context attention kernels (rolled 07:20 PT); rollback resolved the compute blow-up.
- Next actions: Irene will submit an RCA and kernel-change gating checklist; Marissa will submit a support credit request for Tide; we'll schedule a cross-functional retro with Tide next week.

Please reach out immediately if anything else looks off — otherwise I'll move the incident to "post-incident review" and circulate the runbook and RCA draft by EOD PST.

Thanks again for the rapid approvals — saved Tide's cohort launch.

-David
